name: Anteon (Ddosify)
what_it_is: Anteon is an eBPF-based Kubernetes monitoring and load-testing platform (formerly Ddosify). It auto-generates service maps of K8s clusters without code instrumentation and runs scenario-based HTTP/HTTPS/HTTP2 performance tests via a no-code scenario builder.
components: HammerDebug — debug load generator (ddosify/selfhosted_hammer with IS_DEBUG=true)
Celery workers and beat schedulers (backend, alaz-backend, hammermanager)
measurement: Total iteration count and pass/fail rate
Per-step response times and status codes
Kubernetes cluster CPU, memory, disk, and network usage (real-time)
Service-to-service latency via eBPF service map
Prometheus metrics (scraped from all services via prometheus.yml)
configuration: CLI flags: -t (target URL), -n (iteration count), -d (duration seconds), -m (HTTP method), -b (body), -a (basic auth), -h (headers), -T (timeout), -P (proxy), -o (output format), -l (load type), --config (JSON config file), --cert_path, --cert_key_path, --debug
JSON scenario config file with multi-step flows, correlation, CSV test data, cookies, and assertions
Dynamic variables / parameterization in URL, headers, body, and auth (e.g. {{_randomInt}}, {{_randomCity}})
Environment variables loaded via selfhosted/.env file (shared across all backend services)
InfluxDB initialized with org=ddosify, bucket=hammerBucket via DOCKER_INFLUXDB_INIT_* env vars
Prometheus config at init_scripts/prometheus/prometheus.yml; 10-day TSDB retention
fault_injection: No native fault/chaos injection capability documented; tool is a load generator, not a fault injector
Proxy flag (-P) allows routing through an intercepting proxy to simulate network conditions
modes: linear — constant request rate across the duration (default)
debug — single iteration with curl-like verbose output (--debug flag)
constraints: Supports only HTTP, HTTPS, and HTTP/2 protocols; other protocols listed as 'on the way'
Self-hosted stack requires Docker and Docker Compose; Kubernetes monitoring requires deploying the Alaz eBPF agent separately into the target cluster
eBPF-based service map requires Linux kernel with eBPF support; not available on Windows or macOS nodes
CLI output formats limited to stdout and stdout-json; no native HTML/PDF report
Minimum Go 1.18 required to build from source
Low iteration count with long duration may cause the test to finish earlier than expected (linear mode)
docker_services: backend-celery-worker — async task worker for backend
backend-celery-beat — periodic task scheduler for backend
alaz-backend (ddosify/selfhosted_alaz_backend:2.3.11) — eBPF monitoring API on port 8009
alaz-backend-request-writer — writes captured eBPF request data
hammermanager (ddosify/selfhosted_hammermanager:2.0.2) — test orchestration API on port 9901
influxdb (influxdb:2.6.1-alpine) — time-series metrics store on port 9086
seaweedfs (chrislusf/seaweedfs:3.64) — S3-compatible object storage on port 8333
notable_absences: No gRPC or WebSocket protocol support at time of documentation
No built-in distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry/Jaeger/Zipkin) integration in the engine
No native Grafana service in docker-compose (Prometheus data must be visualized externally)
No TLS termination in docker-compose (nginx config is plain reverse proxy, no HTTPS on the self-hosted UI)
No authentication/RBAC documented for the self-hosted web UI
